claims.summary: The origin makes the sponsor of an electioneering communication liable, and a medium liable only if it removes disclosures or alters content into synthetic media; the descendant lacks this.
The descendant creates an action for digital impersonation by candidates or citizens, with a two-year limit, proof elements, and suits on paid ads only against the ad's originator or payer.
The origin treats an interactive computer service as publisher of others' information; the descendant bars digital impersonation actions against it for publishing such information.
The descendant sets fast-track declaratory relief procedures, limits on damages and injunctions, standards of proof, venue, jury rights, and defines digital impersonation and public office.
